title: Open an app blocked by 'cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified'
summary: macOS blocks some apps because it cannot verify their developer. You can allow this one app once from Finder or System Settings, and Gatekeeper stays on for everything else.

error_patterns: cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified
prerequisites: You downloaded the app from its developer's official website or another source you trust
You are logged in as the Mac's administrator if System Settings asks for a password

steps.explain: Check what macOS thinks of the app. This only reads the verdict and changes nothing. A blocked app is reported as rejected.

placeholders.name: APP_PATH
placeholders.description: Full path to the .app bundle that macOS blocks

steps.expect: For a blocked app: a line ending in rejected, often followed by a source= line. The command exits with code 3 when the assessment is denied.

steps.explain: Approve this one app once. Gatekeeper stays on for every other app. Use the first route; if it is missing, use the System Settings route.
steps.gui: Finder: Control-click the app > Open > Open. If there is no Open button (macOS 15 or later), double-click the app, close the warning, then go to System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, click Open Anyway next to the app's name, and confirm with your password or Touch ID.

warnings: Approve only apps whose source you trust. The warning appears because macOS cannot verify who made the app.
Do not turn Gatekeeper off for the whole Mac just to open one app; that lowers protection for every app.
Open Anyway is offered only for a short time after the blocked attempt. If it has gone, double-click the app again.
